pzaecModpackProgressionBundleDesc:
[5ECFFF]Modpack roadmap[-]
This is not a mandatory story campaign, but a set of signposts for the modpack’s main progression branches. The trader gives it after the Project Z survival introduction. Open the bundle and keep the chapters: [FFD866]New Home[-] and [FFD866]Resources Collector[-] start immediately alongside the AEC Garage, Market, Research, Archive and Radiation Threat branches. The native Better Weapon chapter is still awarded separately.

Do not discard the starter chapters and do not cancel their one-time quests. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.

pzaecFG_AECEO01Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
AEC primarily reads your [FFD866]Game Stage (GS)[-], not only character level. GS defines the normal AEC tier ceiling for wilderness progression.

[5ECFFF]Reading the tiers[-]
T00-T04 are the early grades: Basic, Feral, Radiated, Charged and Infernal. Full endgame begins at [FFD866]T05 Veteran / GS 600[-] and continues through T15 Mythic / GS 25000.

[5ECFFF]What may use another tier[-]
An active AEC quest POI can use its fixed contract tier. Player-triggered Tier-Regulator Injectors and Tier Wave Contracts also use explicit tiers, but both are GS-gated. Random world events are not allowed to bypass progression; the unsafe absolute-tier AI05 Boss Incursion is disabled in the canon.

[AAAAAA]A temporary encounter tier does not change your actual Game Stage.[-]
pzaecFG_AECEO02Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
AEC deliberately avoids throwing the entire endgame at a new character. At [FFD866]GS 0-99[-], major world systems do not normally select you as a target and enhanced random spawning nearby is blocked.

[5ECFFF]What changes later[-]
At GS 100-599, Heat and Hazard can already operate, but ordinary world spawning should still stay below free T05+ pressure. Around [FFD866]GS 600[-], the main late-game restrictions are lifted.

[5ECFFF]Not absolute immunity[-]
Quest, POI, Blood Moon and other scripted content can follow separate rules. New-player protection mainly governs AEC world-pressure systems.
pzaecFG_AECEO03Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
[FFD866]Heat[-] is local combat pressure. Each eligible kill adds a base [FFD866]0.5% Heat[-], divided by the number of online players. With one player, roughly 200 eligible kills are required to fill an empty scale.

[5ECFFF]Cooling[-]
Decay begins after 60 real seconds without an eligible kill and removes [FFD866]5% per real minute[-]. The warning threshold is 70%; reaching 100% prepares the next Hazard escalation. Heat resets daily around 04:00.

[5ECFFF]Why it matters[-]
Heat and Hazard can raise pressure around active players, but they are separate from quests and Blood Moon progression. Leaving combat quiet or changing area is a valid way to reduce pressure.

[AAAAAA]A completed escalation chain has a 60-real-minute restart cooldown.[-]
pzaecFG_AECEO04Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
If Heat shows how loud the situation is right now, [FFD866]Hazard[-] shows how dangerous the biome has become over time. It is AEC's longer-term memory of repeated escalations.

[5ECFFF]Levels 0-5[-]
Higher Hazard makes future encounters harsher for eligible players. It does not need to drop after one quiet minute; the system requires a real lull.

[5ECFFF]Calming the area[-]
Let Heat cool completely and stop feeding an endless fight. After sustained quiet, Hazard can begin to decrease.
pzaecFG_AECEO05Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
AEC does not use one fixed list of what can spawn right now. The runtime spawner evaluates [FFD866]GS, biome, time, entity density and local restrictions[-], then selects an allowed family and tier.

[5ECFFF]Why encounters vary[-]
The same area can produce different results at different times. Leaders, escorts, density caps and extra pressure are handled separately; some pressure is suppressed near Land Claims.

[5ECFFF]Separate systems[-]
Blood Moon waves, sleepers, quest spawns and scripted entities do not have to follow the same rules as ordinary wilderness spawning.
pzaecFG_AECEO06Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
AEC can launch [FFD866]world events[-] outside normal POI spawning. The AI Master chooses a new event window after roughly [FFD866]300-600 real minutes[-]; events are biome-scoped and have a 10% migration chance after completion. Timers pause while no living player is connected.

[5ECFFF]Active event families[-]
The canon keeps the themed Doomlord, Singerie, Druid, Ghost, Mushroom, Headless and Archer invasions, plus Mega Horde, Heatmap increase/decrease and Ghost-on-kill pressure. Their runtime paths use AEC eligibility/tier resolution rather than an unrestricted absolute boss roll.

[FF8A65]Canonical guard[-]
The generic AI05 Boss Incursion is disabled. Its original absolute T03/T06/T09/T12/T15 roll could bypass GS progression — for example, producing a T09 boss for a roughly GS 350 player. World Events themselves remain enabled.

[AAAAAA]Watch HUD and server messages: they are operational warnings from the live world system.[-]
pzaecFG_AECEO07Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
AEC Nemesis is the native persistent enemy system: each record keeps a name, title, rank, grudges, territory and combat history across restarts.

[5ECFFF]Native pool[-]
The hard pool limit is [FFD866]40 records[-] and refill begins below 30. The configured rank targets are 10 / 10 / 10 / 6 / 5 / 3; they are target weights/quotas for population shaping, not a promise that all 44 target slots can coexist. The hard pool limit takes priority.

[5ECFFF]Special encounter[-]
Nemesis encounters retain the native persistence, revenge, family-vengeance, power-struggle, territory-war and migration mechanics. The Project Z Nemesis controller is not used in this modpack.
pzaecFG_AECEO08Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
AEC Blood Moon uses its own controller for pressure, late tiers and bosses. It is not merely ordinary wilderness spawning with more zombies.

[5ECFFF]What controls difficulty[-]
The system evaluates player readiness and its own wave rules. [FFD866]Heat and Hazard do not directly choose Blood Moon composition[-], so a calm biome does not guarantee an easy horde night.

[5ECFFF]Preparation[-]
Plan around your GS, equipment, ammunition and group strength. A base that easily handles ordinary events may need a different strategy against prolonged boss pressure.
pzaecFG_AECEO09Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Mutation Samples now follow a predictable danger ladder instead of jumping between tiers. [FFD866]T1[-] comes from ordinary, feral, radiated, charged and infernal default zombies. [FFD866]T2[-] comes from AEC EO tiers 05–07 and Project Z radiated/charged elites. [FFD866]T3[-] comes from AEC EO tiers 08–10 and Project Z infernal elites. [FFD866]T4[-] belongs to AEC EO tiers 11–13, while [FFD866]T5[-] is reserved for tiers 14–15 and the most dangerous named bosses.

[5ECFFF]Bosses and minions[-]
Their sample tier still respects progression. A low-tier boss will not hand out endgame samples simply because it has a huge health pool; instead, tougher targets drop more samples of the appropriate tier. Named Project Z bosses have no AEC tier label, so their reward is based on actual health and physical resistance.

[FF8A65]Keep them[-]
Samples and Infected Teeth are progression resources. Do not throw them away.
pzaecFG_AECEO10Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
The retired AEC EO story campaign no longer drives this modpack. After the Project Z introduction, the trader gives the [FFD866]Modpack Progression Guide[-], while mechanics that do not need their own quest are documented in the Field Archive.

[5ECFFF]Using the Archive[-]
Open the Archive Radio and select any guide from the single list. The full text is visible in the recipe description; crafting is optional. A physical copy costs [FFD866]1 paper[-].

[5ECFFF]Updating saves[-]
For major upstream jumps a fresh save is still the safest option. Updates from one canonical modpack release to the next are intended to preserve supported saves unless that release report explicitly says otherwise. Always back up the world, player data and stateful AEC files first.

[FF8A65]Legacy warning[-]
Retired story books, zombie heads, tier-specific AEC tokens and the old compatibility campaign are not part of current progression.
pzaecFG_AECBoss01Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
The [FFD866]Huntsman[-] drone manages the repeatable AEC BOSSES contract system. It is not a story NPC that you finish once; it remains useful throughout the endgame.

[5ECFFF]What contracts do[-]
A mission can lead to a boss, minions, defense, siege, POI scenario or wave battle. Completing one order does not end the system; take another when ready.

[5ECFFF]Before starting[-]
Read the mission type and expected threat. Some contracts are safer to activate away from your main base.
pzaecFG_AECBoss02Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
AEC bosses have [FFD866]families and star tiers[-]. The same family at a higher star is not necessarily the same fight; later versions are substantially more dangerous and feed deeper research progression.

[5ECFFF]Why stars matter[-]
Stars are used in contracts, Connection Cards and research chains. Always check both the family and the specific target tier.

[5ECFFF]Practical result[-]
Comfortably killing an early version does not mean the next star is safe for the same build.
pzaecFG_AECBoss03Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
AEC BOSSES contracts are not all simple “find and kill one boss” missions. The system includes [FFD866]hunts, defense, mixed hordes, POI scenarios, sieges and wave challenges[-].

[5ECFFF]Why it matters[-]
Different scenarios demand different preparation. Defense tests position and repair supplies, hunts test mobility and single-target damage, while long waves test ammunition, healing and base endurance.

[5ECFFF]Read the conditions[-]
Know what you are starting before activation. A contract can be much more dangerous than the familiar name in its title suggests.
pzaecFG_AECBoss04Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
[FFD866]100-wave[-] contracts and other extreme scenarios are optional late-game challenges, not mandatory tutorial steps. They expect a prepared build, deep supplies and sometimes a group.

[5ECFFF]Bring enough[-]
Ammunition, repairs, healing and an escape plan matter more than one more point of paper damage. Choose a location that can actually survive a long battle.

[5ECFFF]Optional content[-]
Skipping such a contract does not break progression. It is extra risk for late rewards and a test of a completed build.
pzaecFG_AECBoss05Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
The [FFD866]Boss Hunter[-] tab does not simply buff you against every boss at once; its branches specialize against specific families. This lets you build toward the threats you actually face.

[5ECFFF]Late ranks[-]
Besides damage and defense, some branches grant specialized resistance to mechanics from a specific boss, including certain radiation effects.

[5ECFFF]Spending points[-]
Do not buy a branch just for its name. Identify the family blocking your progression and specialize for that target.
pzaecFG_AECBoss06Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
[FFD866]Connection Cards[-] link specific boss families and stars to the Zombie Market and research economy. [FFD866]Research Papers[-] are processed data used by deeper research and market recipes.

[5ECFFF]The cycle[-]
You first learn an early family card, then repeat the principle with other targets and star tiers. The card points to a family/star path; Research Papers turn that hunt into further progression.

[5ECFFF]Do not mix the resources[-]
Cards, AEC coins, Mutation Samples and Research Papers have different jobs. A recipe asking for one is not automatically satisfied by another part of the economy.
pzaecFG_AECBoss07Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
The [FFD866]Quest Relay[-] is a home access point for AEC contracts. Its 1★-5★ upgrades progressively open harder quest pools without restoring the old AEC EO story campaign.

[5ECFFF]Progression[-]
Start with the base station and early contracts, then upgrade the relay through the star tiers. Each step raises the ceiling of available hunts.

[5ECFFF]Important[-]
The Relay is part of the repeatable endgame system, not a one-use story prop.
pzaecFG_PZ01Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Normal stamina answers whether you can sprint or swing again right now. [FFD866]Stamina Reserve[-] tracks long-term exhaustion across the whole raid, so normal stamina may refill while the orange reserve meter remains low.

[5ECFFF]What drains it[-]
Long tool use and melee combat gradually wear the character down. Severe depletion leads to fatigue states, so coffee and short pauses cannot replace proper recovery forever.

[5ECFFF]Recovery[-]
Slow down and take a real rest. Endurance and rest-related perks can reduce drain or improve recovery, but the core rule is simple: hard work requires proper downtime.
pzaecFG_PZ02Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
The purple meter shows your [FFD866]remaining stress resistance[-]. Here 100% is healthy; a falling meter means the character is becoming less able to cope with the situation.

[5ECFFF]What causes stress[-]
Darkness, fears, dangerous creatures and especially nearby high-threat enemies can drain it over time. Personal traits can also alter loss and recovery.

[5ECFFF]Recovery[-]
Carry light at night, leave overwhelming danger and give the character a safe break. Killing certain bosses restores some resistance, but sometimes retreating before the meter collapses is the correct play.
pzaecFG_PZ03Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
[FFD866]Hygiene[-] is a real character state, not a decorative meter. You get dirty over time; encumbrance and certain traits can make that happen faster.

[5ECFFF]Why it matters[-]
Poor hygiene gradually starts interfering with the character's overall condition and can combine badly with stress and other problems. It is easier to manage between raids than during a fight.

[5ECFFF]Cleaning up[-]
Use cleansing supplies and a bath. The bath is especially useful at home because it restores hygiene quickly and also participates in recovery from other states.
pzaecFG_PZ04Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Project Z traits are not ordinary perks bought with points. Many reflect the character's behavior: habits, fears and adaptations can appear, strengthen or disappear according to how you play.

[5ECFFF]What they affect[-]
Traits can change reactions to darkness, animals, zombies, fire, pain, dirt, groups and other conditions. Some are useful; others create additional problems.

[5ECFFF]What to do[-]
Check the traits tab occasionally and read the conditions. If a trait is hurting you, the solution may be changing behavior rather than spending another skill point.
pzaecFG_PZ05Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Project Z expands temperature states: severe heat and cold can progress through multiple stages and seriously impair the character before any enemy even arrives.

[5ECFFF]Preparation[-]
Clothing, shelter, fire, water and appropriate consumables matter more than trying to endure the final stage. Some perks and traits gradually improve adaptation to harsh biomes.

[5ECFFF]Survival rule[-]
If the climate is already hurting health or stamina, stabilize first and fight second. Two simultaneous hazards are almost always worse than one.
pzaecFG_PZ06Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Some Project Z creatures inflict [FFD866]poison[-]. This is a separate condition: a medical kit can heal damage, but it does not automatically remove the toxin itself.

[5ECFFF]Why it is dangerous[-]
Poison can worsen and interfere with movement, stamina and your ability to continue a fight. Spamming healing items does not remove the underlying problem.

[5ECFFF]Preparation[-]
Carry [FFD866]Antidote[-] in quick reach when hunting poisonous creatures. Stop the toxin first, then recover from its consequences.
pzaecFG_PZ07: [777777]30.[-] [F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-] | [FFFFFF]Radiation: Exposure, Dose and Damage[-]
pzaecFG_PZ07Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Project Z radiation has three separate layers: [FFD866]active exposure[-], [FFD866]accumulated irradiation[-] and [FFD866]radiation damage[-]. One item cannot solve all three jobs equally well.

[5ECFFF]Protection[-]
Complete RadProtect sets, certain armor sets and specific perks suppress active radiation effects. Fast Adaptation mainly reduces radiation damage rather than deleting an accumulated dose.

[5ECFFF]Cleansing[-]
ANTIRAD immediately removes part of the accumulated irradiation and accelerates recovery. Cleansing kits improve natural dose removal once active exposure is under control. The Radiation Threat quest branch teaches the basic and improved protection sets.
pzaecFG_PZ08Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
[FFD866]Universal Parts[-] replace a collection of old specialized Project Z components with a common material that returns to advanced crafting later.

[5ECFFF]How to get them[-]
Some compatible Project Z equipment and parts can be salvaged back into this resource. Before selling an unfamiliar component for pocket change, check whether it can be recycled.

[5ECFFF]Why keep them[-]
They are not junk or a one-use quest item. Universal Parts return in advanced technology recipes, so keeping a reserve at home is worthwhile.
pzaecFG_PZ09: [777777]14.[-] [F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-] | [FFFFFF]Project Z Biomes and Creatures[-]
pzaecFG_PZ09Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Project Z creatures are not distributed evenly across the world in this modpack. Their share depends on both [FFD866]biome and Game Stage[-], so the pine forest and late-game wasteland behave very differently.

[5ECFFF]Biome ladder[-]
The pine forest is the softest profile: PZ enemies are rare and PZ bosses are excluded from ordinary wilderness spawning. Burnt Forest, Desert and Snow progressively increase elite and boss pressure, while the [FFD866]Wasteland[-] allows the broadest and most dangerous mix.

[5ECFFF]Why exceptions happen[-]
Sleeper, quest and scripted spawning is handled separately. An unusual enemy inside a POI or event does not necessarily violate the biome rules.
pzaecFG_PZ11Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Project Z Rare Contracts are separate from AEC missions. At the [FFD866]Radio Station[-], you spend [FFD866]Quest Notes[-] to obtain a bundle containing one random mission from the restored pool of [FFD866]21 contracts[-].

[5ECFFF]Rewards[-]
Completing them leads to special ingredients used for elixirs. Some rewards are much stronger than ordinary consumables and belong to late-game progression.

[5ECFFF]Separate systems[-]
A Project Z Rare Contract and an AEC Huntsman contract can exist at the same time. They use different items and reward paths.
pzaecFG_PZ12Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Late progression outgrows the vanilla workbench. Project Z uses improved crafting stations and specialized station tools, so a familiar-looking recipe can require completely different infrastructure.

[5ECFFF]If a recipe seems missing[-]
Check the [FFD866]required station, station tool, relevant skill and progression requirement[-]. Some late chemistry, equipment and special components simply cannot be made at a basic workbench.

[5ECFFF]Keep useful infrastructure[-]
A new station often complements the old one rather than making it instantly obsolete. Check which recipes truly moved to the new technology tier.
pzaecFG_PZ13Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Not every infected creature uses the same reward path. Eligible humanoid targets can directly grant a [FFD866]Mutation Sample[-], [FFD866]Infected Teeth[-] and a [FFD866]Zombie Corpse[-] when killed.

[5ECFFF]The corpse bundle[-]
The Zombie Corpse is a separate biological-resource container that can be opened later instead of forcing you to harvest every humanoid body on the spot.

[5ECFFF]Infected animals[-]
Zombie animals and other infected animal types generally remain in the normal harvesting system. A wolf or bear not dropping the humanoid reward set is expected behavior.
pzaecFG_PZ14Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Rest in Project Z is more than passing time. Bedrolls, mattresses and beds help recover [FFD866]Stamina Reserve[-] and stress resistance, with proper sleeping arrangements generally providing better recovery than a brief pause.

[5ECFFF]Bathing[-]
A bath restores hygiene quickly and also contributes to relaxation and cleansing. Before a long raid, recover at home; full normal stamina does not mean the character is fully rested.

[5ECFFF]Practical advice[-]
When several condition meters are low at once, do not try to fix them in the middle of combat. Return somewhere safe, rest, wash up and head out again prepared.
pzaecFG_PZ15Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
Project Z farming goes beyond ordinary plots. Skills, specialized equipment and late stations make food production more stable and less dependent on a lucky harvest.

[5ECFFF]Hydroponics[-]
The [FFD866]Hydroponic Station[-] is a separate accelerated growing cycle for supported crops. It is not a universal box for every seed; available crops and efficiency depend on progression.

[5ECFFF]If a recipe is locked[-]
Check farming perks and station requirements. Often the recipe is not missing; the corresponding production tier simply has not been unlocked yet.
pzaecFG_PZ16Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
The reactor drill, driver and related infrastructure form a separate late Project Z energy branch. For these tools, [FFD866]durability effectively acts as charge[-], not merely wear.

[5ECFFF]Charging[-]
Dedicated charging stations restore energy from the electrical grid. If a reactor tool appears “broken” after use, check its charging infrastructure before reaching for an ordinary repair kit.

[5ECFFF]Plan base power[-]
Portable reactors, reactor batteries and charging stations belong to the same technology cycle. The more reactor equipment you use, the more important planned power generation becomes.
pzaecGuideRadiation01Desc:
[90FF75]Radiation Threat 1/2 — Protection[-]
Project Z separates active radiation exposure, accumulated irradiation and radiation damage. The first protection kit teaches how to suppress active exposure and how ANTIRAD removes part of an already accumulated dose.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Collect all four basic [FFD866]RadProtect[-] armor modifications and [FFD866]ANTIRAD[-].

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest and do not discard its linked chapter or quest item. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
pzaecGuideRadiation02Desc:
[90FF75]Radiation Threat 2/2 — Maximum Protection[-]
Improved RadProtect plates add another protection layer. Irradiated Shell is an emergency stimulant that temporarily prevents new irradiation accumulation, but ends with a 25% irradiation backlash.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Collect all four improved [FFD866]RadProtect[-] plates and [FFD866]Irradiated Shell[-].

[FF8A65]Important[-]

startQuest1Offer:

Project Z begins with a short survival introduction rather than the endgame. It establishes the character’s starting point and then hands out three survival chapters in sequence.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Complete the introduction. The next chapter is [FFD866]Self-Treatment[-].

[FF8A65]Important[-]

startQuest2Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [FF6666]Survival 1/3 — Self-Treatment[-]

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Let the short sequence finish. You will receive a first-aid bandage and the next chapter.

[FF8A65]Important[-]

startQuest3Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [FF6666]Survival 2/3 — The Attacker[-]

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill the spawned infected and take the final chapter of the message.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
startQuest4Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [FF6666]Survival 3/3 — Reach a Trader[-]
The final note sends you to any trader. That meeting ends the introduction and opens the modpack’s free-form progression.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Reach a trader and speak with them. Alongside starting supplies you will receive the [FFD866]Modpack Progression Guide[-] and the opening Project Z weapon chapter.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
ResCollector1Offer:

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill [FFD866]5 infected from the worker family[-], collect [FFD866]250 scrap iron[-], [FFD866]50 wood[-] and [FFD866]5 short iron pipes[-], craft the matching ingredient package and bring it to a trader. The reward is a choice of an iron tool.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
ResCollector2Offer:

The reward is a choice of an improved power tool.

ResCollector5Offer:

The reward is a choice of a reactor auger or reactor impact driver.

ResCollector6Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [FAFF63]Resource Collector 6/6 — Charging Station[-]

NewHome1Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [FF7E2F]New Home 1/4 — Shelter[-]
Start with a simple wooden shelter. The point is not architecture; it is learning the bulk building and upgrade loop.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Place [FFD866]100 frame blocks[-], upgrade [FFD866]100 frames[-], then return to the trader.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
NewHome2Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [FF7E2F]New Home 2/4 — Stronger Walls[-]
Wood is fine for a start, but not for a serious siege. The next step is stronger masonry and sturdier entrances.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Upgrade [FFD866]100 wooden blocks[-] plus one wooden door and one wooden hatch, then return to the trader.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
NewHome3Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [FF7E2F]New Home 3/4 — Bunker[-]
Now the base moves into concrete and heavy entrances, a fortification tier meant for much more dangerous attacks.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Upgrade [FFD866]100 cobblestone blocks[-], [FFD866]2 iron hatches[-] and [FFD866]2 iron doors[-], then return to the trader.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
NewHome4Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [FF7E2F]New Home 4/4 — Bomb Shelter[-]
The final chapter moves the fortification into steel and powered entrances. This completes the basic Project Z building ladder.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Upgrade [FFD866]100 concrete blocks[-] and place [FFD866]2 powered vault doors[-] plus [FFD866]2 powered vault hatches[-].

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
BetterWeaponMeleeT1Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — First Milestone[-]
The first weapon milestone does not require a specific weapon type; it measures combat experience. It opens the ranged chapter plus a choice between light and heavy melee branches.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill [FFD866]75 infected[-] and return to the trader.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
BetterWeaponMeleeLightT1Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Light Melee I[-]
This is the light-melee reward branch. The objective does not require a specific weapon, so use whatever keeps you alive.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill [FFD866]50 infected[-] and choose knuckles, a knife or a robotic sledge as the reward.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
BetterWeaponMeleeHeavyT1Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Heavy Melee I[-]

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill [FFD866]50 infected[-] and choose a spear, club or sledgehammer as the reward.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
BetterWeaponRangeT1Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Ranged I[-]
The first ranged milestone also counts ordinary kills without requiring a specific weapon class. The reward is one of the starting ranged sets.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill [FFD866]100 infected[-], return to the trader and choose one ranged reward.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
BetterWeaponMeleeT2Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Steel Milestone[-]
The second melee milestone again measures overall combat progress, then opens stronger light/heavy melee rewards and the next ranged chapter.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill [FFD866]150 infected[-] and return to the trader.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
BetterWeaponMeleeLightT2Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Light Melee II[-]
The second light-melee branch leads to the next weapon tier. As before, the kill counter itself is not weapon-class restricted.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill [FFD866]100 infected[-] and choose steel knuckles, a machete or a stun baton.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
BetterWeaponMeleeHeavyT2Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Heavy Melee II[-]
The second heavy-melee branch leads to steel weapons. The kills can be made however you prefer; the branch determines the reward.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill [FFD866]100 infected[-] and choose a steel spear, steel club or steel sledgehammer.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
BetterWeaponRangeT2Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Ranged II[-]
The second ranged milestone improves the reward tier and leads toward the military milestone. The kill counter is not restricted to a weapon class.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Kill [FFD866]250 infected[-], then choose one ranged reward set.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
Do not cancel this one-time quest or discard its linked chapter. Restoring a lost chain may require an administrator.
BetterWeaponRangeT3Offer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Military Milestone[-]
This quest splits a large kill total into three sequential phases. There is no held-weapon restriction; the combined requirement is 450 kills.

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]
Complete three phases of [FFD866]150 kills[-] each and return to the trader.

BetterWeaponImpModsOffer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Improved Modifications[-]

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]

BetterWeaponMeleeImpModsOffer:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [DECEA3]Better Weapons — Improved Melee Mods[-]

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]

BetterWeaponRangeImpModsOffer:

BetterWeaponUniqueModsOffer:

[5ECFFF]Objective[-]

[FF8A65]Important[-]

pzaecFG_AECEO11Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
The [FFD866]Zombie Market[-] is the central AEC logistics station in this modpack. Its main request currency is [FFD866]Infected Teeth[-]: you generally order delivery or infrastructure rather than buying the final item directly.

[5ECFFF]What grows through the market[-]
Server batteries, cryptomining, Connection Cards, AEC coins, Research Papers, passive production and part of the late-game supply chain begin here. Many entries have multiple sizes or tiers.

[5ECFFF]Reading requests[-]
An item marked as an Airdrop Request is not automatically the final battery, station or resource crate. Obtain the request, then complete its delivery cycle where applicable.
pzaecFG_AECEO13Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]

[5ECFFF]Where to get it[-]
Complete the AEC contracts available through the supported quest systems. Harder contracts generally award more, so your token reserve grows together with late-game capability.

[FF8A65]Do not discard them[-]
Universal Tokens are a progression resource, separate from trader currency, AEC coins and Infected Teeth.
pzaecFG_AECEO14Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
The [FFD866]Necroforge[-] is a late AEC station that transmutes ordinary ammunition into tiered combat bundles. It does not replace the normal workbench; it becomes valuable once you can reliably acquire Mutation Samples.

[5ECFFF]Recipes[-]
Bring ordinary ammunition of the required caliber plus samples of the appropriate value, and the station creates a bundle for the selected tier. Higher tiers cost progressively more.

[5ECFFF]When to build it[-]
The branch opens near early mutator progression. If samples are still scarce, establish the research economy before feeding them into ammunition conversion.
pzaecFG_PZ17Desc:
[F87C63][Project Z][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]

[5ECFFF]The three main stimulants[-]
[FFD866]Equilibrium[-] prevents knockdown and stun. [FFD866]Clear Gaze[-] blocks vision-altering effects. [FFD866]Irradiated Shell[-] temporarily stops radiation accumulation and speeds cleansing, but ends with a [FF8A65]+25% irradiation backlash[-].

[5ECFFF]When to use them[-]
Know the threat you are countering. Experimental medicine is strongest when used for a specific hazard, not as a replacement for preparation.

[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
[FFD866]Tier Wave Contracts[-] are repeatable combat trials from T00 through T15. Activating one starts a scripted five-wave assault: 10 hostiles per wave, with the next group arriving after 60 seconds even if the previous wave is still alive.

[5ECFFF]Progression gate[-]
Crafting and activation require the corresponding AEC tier: T00 GS 0, T01 100, T02 200, T03 300, T04 400, T05 600, T06 1200, T07 2000, T08 3200, T09 5000, T10 7500, T11 10500, T12 14000, T13 18000, T14 22000 and T15 25000.

[5ECFFF]Cost[-]
Contracts are produced in the [FFD866]Zombie Market[-] quest tab from Generic Research Papers using the canonical 1/2/3-paper pattern within each three-tier band; T15 uses one Generic 5 paper.

[FF8A65]Important[-]
The waves are scripted and do not use ordinary biome SpawnRules. The contract therefore checks the activating player's unlocked tier. There is no automatic Universal Token reward: the reward is the encounter, normal kill XP and normal kill loot.

pzaecFG_AECEO17Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
[FFD866]LootStage (LS)[-] controls loot selection independently from Game Stage. In the canon, legitimate high LootStage is preserved: values above 500 are not intentionally reduced to 500.

[5ECFFF]High-LS policy[-]
Affected loot groups and containers are extended to the canonical range up to [FFD866]999999[-]. Containers that must preserve the real LootStage receive targeted handling instead of a global clamp. This prevents high-LS characters from falling past the last defined loot range and receiving worse or empty results.

[5ECFFF]Safety guard[-]
The AEC compatibility guard remains active only as an emergency ceiling: ordinary values such as 501, 1000, 4532 or 50000 pass through unchanged; only pathological values above 999999 are capped.

[FF8A65]If loot becomes worse as LS rises[-]
Report the exact container, your LootStage and the POI/biome. The correct fix is the affected loot table, not resetting the character or restoring the old LS 500 clamp.
pzaecFG_AECEO18Desc:
[FFD700][AEC][-] [66B3FF]Field Guide[-]
[FFD866]Biome Challenge Baits[-] are utility recipes in a dedicated Mutation Incubator tab. Four baits cover the archetypes used by biome trials: Burnt Zombie / Burnt Forest, Rancher / Desert, Chuck / Snow and Mutated Zombie / Wasteland.

[5ECFFF]How it works[-]
Craft a lure, use it to start a short repeatable quest, then place the supplied marker in the correct biome. There is no Rally Point. Placement itself completes the utility quest and its completion event triggers exactly 10 aggressive challenge-only enemies at roughly 15–25 m. No turn-in is required.

[5ECFFF]Anti-abuse policy[-]
Lured aliases give 0 kill XP, have 0 loot-bag chance, are absent from ConfigurableKillRewards and deliberately lack normal Project Z archetype tags. Corpses remain only briefly. The quest itself has no rewards. Each bait always costs the equivalent of 200 Tier-1 Mutation Samples: Smelting consumes 200 internal T1 reserve units, while Recipes consumes 200 physical T1 sample items from player inventory. A hidden per-player 60-second activation cooldown is refreshed again when the bait is placed, limiting rapid quest-spawn chaining.

[AAAAAA]The intended biome challenge still owns progression: these enemies are added only to its exact entity list and the biome condition remains active.[-]
